concepts.why: Academic scholar / all: Deut 18:5 names Levi and his sons 'to stand and minister', not priests; it already sits under 'To stand before the LORD to serve Him'.
Academic scholar: 1 Kgs 8:11 is the cloud of glory stopping the priests from ministering, not carrying the ark; it is already carried by the secondary 'Glory' node.

concepts.name: A breastpiece of judgment, the Urim and Thummim
concepts.why: Academic scholar: Num 27:21, Deut 33:8 and Ezra 2:63 name the Urim and Thummim but not the breastpiece, so the old name says more than half its passages; Exod 28:12 is the shoulder pieces of the ephod, not the breastpiece (28:29-30 carry the point). Optional additions in the texts' words: 1 Sam 23:9-12 and 30:7-8 (the ephod brought, the LORD asked).

Lutheran / Baptist / Catholic / Reformed (parting on whether 'bodies washed with pure water' is baptism): set under the priests' bronze basin it makes the New Testament washing the counterpart of the priests' washing, which is a typological claim no passage here makes, and it names no basin or priest. It stays, as the text, under 'Draw near to God'.

Academic scholar: Heb 8:3 says the high priest offers 'gifts and sacrifices' and then turns to what 'this One' has to offer; it does not say a priest makes atonement, and Heb 5:1 already carries the Hebrews side. Catholic / Reformed: with it dropped the concept stays description of the Levitical priest and leaves the ministerial-priesthood question open.

concepts.name: The fire on the altar, every morning and every evening
concepts.why: Academic scholar: only Lev 6:9-13 speak of the fire kept burning; Lev 9:24 is fire from the LORD, and Exod 29:38-39 and 2 Chr 13:11 are the daily offerings. The name should cover all six, in 2 Chr 13:11's words.

concepts.name: To burn incense before the LORD
concepts.why: Academic scholar: Lev 16:12-13 is a censer from the bronze altar, and 1 Chr 23:13, 2 Chr 26:18, Luke 1:9, Ps 141:2 and Rev 8:3 do not mention an altar of incense at all; only Exod 30:1 and 30:7-8 do. 'Burn incense before the LORD' (1 Chr 23:13) says what every passage says.

concepts.name: The high priest and the priests in the Gospels and Acts
concepts.why: Academic scholar / Jewish reader of the texts: Mark 14:61, Acts 6:7 and Acts 23:4-5 name neither Annas nor Caiaphas (Acts 23 is another high priest), and Acts 6:7 is a great number of priests believing, so the old name says more than three of its eight passages. A plain label covers the whole set, including the priests who 'became obedient to the faith', without making the concept a list of those who stood against Jesus.

note_fixes: Deuteronomy 14:29: the note says nothing of the tithe and names only the foreigner, orphan and widow; use 'the Levite (because he has no portion or inheritance among you)', or cite 14:28-29 so that 'a tenth of all your produce' is in the passage
concepts.why: Academic scholar: the note must show the concept it sits under; as written it leaves out the Levite, who is the reason the verse is here.

concepts.name: The covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites
concepts.why: Academic scholar: 'My covenant with Levi' (Mal 2:4) is not what Num 25:12-13 says; there the covenant of permanent priesthood is given to Phinehas and his descendants. Neh 13:29 ('the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites') holds all seven passages without merging two covenants the texts name separately.

concepts.name: A faithful priest
concepts.why: Jewish / academic / Catholic-Orthodox-Reformed readers all: 'I will raise up for Myself a faithful priest' (1 Sam 2:35) set as the name over Heb 2:17 and 3:1-2 says the promise is answered by Jesus, and the rule forbids a concept saying one Testament is fulfilled in the other. 'A faithful priest' is the phrase both texts share and claims no more; 1 Sam 2:35 and the Mal 2:6 portrait stay beside Hebrews. 1 Sam 2:30 is the general warning to Eli's house, not a faithful priest.

note_fixes: Isaiah 61:10: use 'He has clothed me with garments of salvation and wrapped me in a robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom wears a priestly headdress'; the current note shows only the headdress and not the clothing the name is about
concepts.why: Academic scholar: the note must carry the name's 'clothed with righteousness / salvation'.

concepts.name: Melchizedek
concepts.why: Jewish / academic / Catholic / Baptist-dispensational / Reformed (the tradition parting this theme most): Gen 14:18-19 says Melchizedek was priest of God Most High, not 'forever', and the old name makes the whole chain one thing before the reader has read it; Ps 110:4 and Hebrews 5-7 say 'forever'. A plain label lets each passage say its own and keeps the Genesis account, the psalm and Hebrews side by side with no claim that one is the other's fulfilment. Each note is an exact quotation; none should be reworded.

Academic scholar: Rom 12:1 and Heb 13:15 say believers offer sacrifices, but neither says priesthood; they share the sacrifice word with 1 Pet 2:5. Setting them under 'A royal priesthood' reads them as the common priesthood, which is the very point the Lutheran, Reformed and Baptist readers (priesthood of all believers) and the Catholic and Orthodox readers (a common and a ministerial priesthood) take differently. Moved to a new concept, 'A sacrifice of praise' (see missing), they need no claim.

secondary_or_links: Secondary concepts: accept as drafted. The eight nodes are cut to verses, none claims one Testament fulfils the other, and the dark side is not softened (Jer 23:11, Micah 3:11).

Link 'Law/Wisdom': check that this is the live label. The recently published themes are 'The Law' and 'Wisdom Literature'; if they are two themes the link should be one or both of those names, not a slash-joined label.
Links to 'Church' and 'Messiah/Christology': no change, provided they are the site's own theme labels; they name the theme and say nothing about whether one fulfils the other.

Concept 38 (You priests who despise My name) should take more of the dark side so that making the last concept a blessing softens nothing: Jeremiah 2:8, Isaiah 28:7, Hosea 6:9, and Ezekiel 44:10-13 (the Levites who strayed and bear their iniquity). 1 Sam 2:27-36 (the word against Eli's house, of which 2:35 is a part) belongs here as well, so that the promise in 'A faithful priest' is not read without the sentence it answers.

Order: the last concept is the theme's own words of hope, from within the theme (Num 6:24-26 and the priests' blessing), and the dark concepts (12, 35, 38) are kept. Accept. The Hebrews run (42-45) followed by 46-49 reads as a sequence, but it is also chronological and ends on Aaron's blessing, and Jer 33:18 and Ezek 44 are kept earlier; no reader should take a side from it.

missing.why: A reader would expect it: Ezek 44:15 is cited under two concepts but the Zadokite priests and the Levites who 'went far from Me' (44:10-14) are the text's distinction between priests and Levites, and the second set is a dark word the theme should not leave out. Dispensational and other readers will look for Ezek 40-48, so give it with no comment on how it is to be read.
The counterpart of 'The LORD is their inheritance': no land, but forty-eight towns with pastureland. Numbers 35 is already cited only for the death of the high priest.

missing.sub_theme: To invoke, to thank and to praise the LORD
missing.why: The Levite singers and musicians are a plain strand of the texts; the theme has only the trumpets, and this is the Levites' work most of the later books describe.

Hebrews 7 is cut to 7:1-3, 7:15-16 and the verses of other concepts, so the text's own statement of the contrast is absent, and Jewish and dispensational readers will notice Hebrews is quoted only where it is gentle. Give it as the text's words (7:11 'when there is a change in the priesthood, there must also be a change in the law' is for the writer to confirm) with no gloss on what is changed or who it is for.
Takes in the sacrifice passages removed from 'A royal priesthood' and the psalms the theme already draws on; the texts develop what the worshipper offers in more than one book.
The return lists and Joshua and Ezra the priest are how the post-exile books themselves speak of priests; only Ezra 2:62-63 and Neh 13 appear now.

The one place where priests are slain: Saul has eighty-five of them killed. The Bread of the Presence concept cites 21:6, and the theme should not show only the priests who fail, never the ones who suffer.
